4. **What M6 is.** A renovation program of the whole codebase in slices (D-WORKFLOW-181; the order `docs/reviews/order.md`, the slice table `docs/reviews/slices.json`). This session is the **coordinator lane** (D-WORKFLOW-183): it researches and writes each slice's brief, has a stranger prove it, dispatches it to a work lane, accepts each stage, triages the acceptance runs, ticks the criteria, closes, verifies the close-out. **It never edits a lane's worktree** (reads by `git -C <path> show <hash>:<file>` only), except the dispatch seed and a hand-back merge the lane performs itself. Planning, criteria, briefs, Backlogs, register rows and rule edits are the coordinator's; lanes execute and file their own audit issue and bugs (D-WORKFLOW-189).
5. **The work lanes are herdr sessions** in the workspace "pixelelated · Codebase renovation": address them with `herdr agent prompt <name> "<text>"` and read their state with `herdr agent list` (`agent_status`: `working` / `done` / `idle`). Every answer to a lane is a comment on its issue **and** a prompt; a lane's turn ends on a question or a checkpoint post, never on a progress post. Lane names: `m6-t1-os-launch` (the T1 session), `m6-t3-emulators` (T3), `m6-t5-build-engine` (T5); `m6-p1-survey` and `m6-t2-es-launch` are older, idle, unassigned.
6. **The coordinator's tools live outside the tree**, in `/workspace/tmp/m6-coordinator/kit/` (unversioned; Backlog #1386 is to give them a tree home): the acceptance scripts (`t36-accept.sh` is the shared code at sha256 prefix `e32e28e014557000`; per-slice scripts are derived by `kit/selftest/accept-tNN/derive-tNN.py` and refuse on any undefined constant), the tick scripts and maps (`tNN-tick.py`, `tNN-ticks.md`), the research and proof files, `ledger-union.py`, `mask.sed`, `host-ack.sh`, `compile-ack.sh`, and `monitors.md` (the watches to re-arm). **One agent at a time edits `t36-accept.sh`**; a derivation is re-run after it moves.
7. **The host is shared with the M7 lane** through `/workspace/tmp/m7-m6-host-coordination.txt` (767 lines at the stash): one runtime at a time; M7's START/RETURN lines are acknowledged within seconds by `kit/compile-ack.sh` (alive, pid 4189276, below); M6 runs no compile over an open M7 START and posts its own compile START/END through `kit/t36-compile-run.sh`'s shape. **At the stash M7 has a guest running** (START 13:13:00 `RA stable-on-fr640`, its own `watch-job` and QEMU), acknowledged at 13:13; M6 holds no START.
